title: Atman: a Rust command-line toolkit for reproducible proteomics analysis
description: Atman is a command-line toolkit for proteomics analysis, written in Rust. It ingests protein matrices from Olink Explore, SomaScan, MaxQuant, DIA-NN and Spectronaut into one canonical TSV schema and runs the same commands on all of them: QC, differential abundance (paired, Welch, OLS, mixed, limma, DEqMS, msqrob, ensemble), module discovery and testing, enrichment, decomposition (ICA, NMF, unmixing, variance partition), cross-cohort alignment, harmonisation, and subject-level bootstrap and null calibration. Every command writes a run sidecar that records the binary, the build environment, and SHA-256 digests of inputs and outputs. Statistical paths are validated against R reference implementations in CI. The code is dual licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 at the user's option. Zenodo records a single identifier, so MIT is given here. The bundled Dube et al. 2023 Olink Explore fixture data are redistributed under CC BY 4.0 from Figshare project 163291.
